stage1.impression: A warm, timber-lined listening bar with a convincing mood: the low beamed ceiling, the lit record wall and the pendants pooling light on the counter feel right for a kissa-style room. But two large translucent ghost figures are laid over both speaker niches and read as a double exposure stacked in post, not as a quarter-second blur. They hide the speakers, so the hero is lost. The counter top is a flat, pale, plaster-like slab with no zinc sheen, and the record wall repeats like a tiled texture. As it stands, a magazine would see a generic, well-lit CG bar and not a specific place: the altar-like speakers, which would make it specific, cannot be read.

blocking_9: Both EARF speakers are legible at a glance, with nothing passing in front of them: the niche interiors [170,300,340,540] and [700,330,770,480] show the dark smoked cabinet and woofer, not a pale ghost (lum_median under 80 there today, 144 and 163)
Motion blur reads as a photographic long exposure, with the moving person's body mostly opaque and only its edges smeared, not as a uniform half-transparent overlay
The counter top reads as patinated zinc: darker, with a soft reflection of the pendants and wear, not as a matte pale-grey slab (lum_median 177 now)
The horn mouth in the left niche [240,140,345,220] shows no blown white triangle (p95 240.6)
The record wall shows varied spines (colour, height, a few face-out sleeves, gaps) with no visible repetition
The pendant shades hold detail and do not clip (clip 1.01 % in [380,200,485,262])

defects.what: Large translucent ghost guest in front of the left speaker niche. It reads as a composited double exposure and hides the speaker
A second ghost figure overlaps the right speaker niche. The speaker cannot be read
Ghost seated guest at the right edge with a pale smeared head. The blur is uniform and translucent, not photographic
Blown white triangular area inside the horn/niche top reads as a hole or a light leak
Counter top is a flat, pale-grey, uniform surface. It reads as plaster or a CG plane, not zinc. No reflections of the pendants and no wear
Record spines are evenly sized and evenly toned, like a tiled texture. They read as a texture and not as a collection
Nearest pendant shade clips (1.01 %) and reads as opal white plastic
The record player and glass boxes on the counter are small and grey and do not read as products
Fine uniform grain over smooth surfaces plus denoiser smear inside the ghost figures
Foreground chair backs are cut by the frame edge and have smooth, untextured leather

changes.problem: The blurred guests stand directly in front of both speaker niches, so the hero products are hidden behind pale translucent smears.

evidence.measured: lum_median 143.8 with r/g/b 163/140/123 inside the left niche, where a smoked cabinet should be dark. The right niche [700,330,770,480] has lum_median 162.8

change.setting: people: places (3 at the counter, the bartender)
change.from: guest and bartender placed between the camera and the two back-bar niches
change.to: the bartender moved to the gap between the niches behind the decks; the counter guests seated at the near and far ends of the counter, none on the line of sight to either niche

changes.expected: Both speakers are seen whole in their niches: the dark smoked acrylic, the woofer and the horn are legible. The niche interiors drop to about 50 to 80.

changes.problem: The motion blur is a uniform half-transparent overlay, the look of a composite and not of a quarter-second exposure, where a seated body stays mostly solid and only the moving head and hands smear.

evidence.measured: the seated guest's head and arm are see-through, with the wall visible through them. The left figure's arm is a 250 px pale smear

change.from: shutter 1.0 frame; travel [0.2, 0.12, 0.03] m, turn 35 deg
change.to: shutter 0.5 frame; travel [0.06, 0.04, 0.01] m, turn 12 deg; only the bartender's pouring arm moves more

changes.expected: Bodies read as solid, softly blurred people with faces still unreadable. The frame reads as a photograph of a live room.

changes.problem: The zinc counter top reads as a matte pale-grey plaster plane, the brightest large surface in the frame, with no metal sheen, patina or reflection.

evidence.measured: lum_median 177, r/g/b 188/175/161, delta-E 14.8 against an aged-zinc #8A8D8F. The front-edge profile peaks at 195

change.to: aged zinc: base about #7E8286, metallic 0.8, roughness 0.35 with a 0.25 to 0.5 mottled roughness map, darker ring marks and wiping streaks, soft reflections of the Domes

changes.expected: The counter reads as a worn zinc top with soft pools and streaky reflections under each pendant. Its median falls to about 100 to 130.

changes.problem: The speakers are not lit as the altar of the room: no light rakes their smoked acrylic, so their tint and the glow through the cabinet do not read, and a white blown patch sits in the left horn area.

evidence.measured: p95 240.6 against a median of 35.7: one hard white triangle in an otherwise dark horn

change.setting: lamps: on each Ember speaker 4 x area; the lit niche's strip
change.from: 1.0 W/m2 at the target; niche strip 0.12
change.to: 2.5 W/m2 at the target, aimed to graze the cabinet's sides and edges; niche strip 0.05 so it no longer blows out behind the horn

changes.expected: The cabinets' polished edges glow and the smoked tint shows. The horn mouth holds detail with no flat white shape.

changes.problem: The record wall reads as a repeated texture of evenly toned spines, the clearest sign of a render after the ghosts.

evidence.measured: at 1:1, cubby after cubby carries the same pattern of pale spines with the same heights and spacing

change.from: uniform spine set repeated per cubby
change.to: per-cubby random spine colour (mostly pale/black with a few coloured), +/-5 % lean, a few half-empty cubbies, 3 to 4 sleeves turned face-out

changes.expected: The wall reads as a collection built up over years. No pattern repeats in any 1:1 crop.

changes.problem: The nearest Dome shade clips and reads as opal white plastic instead of a glowing frosted liner.

change.setting: EARF's lamps: each Dome's liner glow

changes.expected: The shades glow softly with a visible gradient toward the rim. No clipping.

changes.problem: The objects on the counter are small grey shapes that do not read as EARF's record players or as a night's use, so the counter looks staged and empty.

evidence.measured: at 2x, the R3 Float units read as grey glass boxes with no lit base visible. The coupes sit in a row

change.setting: props and the record player's lit base
change.from: glasses evenly spaced; record player base unlit or faint
change.to: a record out of its sleeve on the near player, the coat over the nearest chair back in frame, glasses grouped unevenly with a wet ring; raise the R3 base glow so the clear posts read

changes.expected: The counter reads as lived-in and the decks read as products.

changes.problem: A fine uniform grain and denoiser smear sit over flat areas, and the right half lies under a grey veil that flattens the room's depth.

evidence.measured: lum_median 32.8 with p5 16.2: lifted, low-contrast blacks in the far room

change.to: haze 0.0025; samples 512 with the same adaptive threshold

changes.expected: Deeper, cleaner blacks in the far room, still with detail, and no grain on the counter or ceiling.

out_of_scope.request: Board-formed concrete and blackened steel visible in this view (the shell reads all timber here)
out_of_scope.why: The room's materials and layout are fixed. Only a camera move could bring them in, and that would change the frame's purpose

out_of_scope.request: Dome shades in a darker smoke so they do not read white
out_of_scope.why: The colour of EARF's lamps is fixed by the configuration
